title: Same musicians in many bands
summary: Why the same men appear on records with different bands.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Well, one thing that keeps coming to my mind, and I'm glad I thought of it before this tape runs out, I noticed, looking at all the old records, which is the only way that I can really look back and remember these fellas, the number of times the same fellas played with different bands. Was it because they were having fights and squabbles and quitting and going to somebody else or what?

Well, uh, if the records were made here, uh, some of these bands still adhered to the old principle. They hired the same man to play with three, four, five different bands because he's good. Uh-huh. Because they think he's the best. Uh-huh. But there is no such a thing as the best.

Well, you know what I'm trying to lead up to is this. You take what's going on in your audience today, it's the same damn thing. You'll find the same musician's name with all different kinds of bands.
Yeah. Because they think he's the best.
No, sometimes you hear him around you, I wouldn't play with so many people.
